name: org.machanism.machai:bindex-mcp-server
description: Bindex MCP Server is a Java 17 standalone Model Context Protocol server distribution that combines org.machanism.machai:bindex-core with the org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server runtime. It exposes Bindex metadata retrieval, metadata registration, schema-oriented descriptor validation, and natural-language library recommendation to MCP-compatible AI clients and automation. Bindex descriptors identify software artifacts through coordinates, versions, purpose, classification, integrations, dependencies, examples, and configuration guidance. The server retrieves complete or GraphQL-style filtered descriptors, registers records supplied as JSON objects, project-relative files, or remote URLs, and recommends reusable libraries from natural-language requirements. Recommendations use AI-generated classifications and embeddings together with language, architectural-layer, similarity-score, and version-aware filtering over a MongoDB-backed repository. The executable entry point is org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer. It communicates through STDIO when no port is supplied, or serves MCP over HTTP at /mcp when started with a port; streamable session-capable HTTP is available with the session option. Configure GenAI and embedding services for registration and semantic recommendation workflows.

usageContext: Automated metadata registration and library recommendation

constructors.description: The packaged application entry point starts the Machai MCP runtime with Bindex capabilities. Without a port option it uses STDIO. A port starts HTTP transport, and the session option enables streamable session-capable HTTP transport.

examples.description: Launch the server as a local STDIO MCP process for the project workspace, then configure an MCP client to communicate with its standard input and output streams.

features.name: Start Bindex MCP server
features.description: Runs the executable Bindex MCP server and publishes Bindex metadata retrieval, registration, and natural-language library recommendation operations. HTTP clients connect to the /mcp endpoint after the server starts with a port.

examples.description: Start stateless HTTP MCP transport on port 8080, then connect a compatible client to http://localhost:8080/mcp to use Bindex operations.
Start streamable session-capable HTTP transport for a client that supports session-aware MCP communication.

features.name: Register and recommend Bindex metadata
features.description: The Bindex Core-backed MCP operations retrieve a descriptor, register a Bindex JSON file or JSON object, and find recommended libraries from a natural-language requirement. Registration normalizes metadata and can generate classification and embeddings. Recommendation uses configured semantic search, repository, and relevance settings.

examples.description: Resolve and run the related Maven plugin, configure it with a readable Machai MCP properties file, then connect an MCP client to register a bindex.json document or request matching libraries.

examples.title: Build, configure, and run a local STDIO MCP server
examples.description: This scenario installs the server from source and lets a local MCP client launch it as a STDIO subprocess for a project workspace.
steps: Install Java 17 or later and Apache Maven.
Clone the project and run mvn clean install from the project root to build the artifact.
Configure MongoDB access through BINDEX_REPO_URL and any required BINDEX_USER and BINDEX_PASSWORD values.

Configure a generation or classification model with gw.model or pick.model and a compatible embedding.model; provide provider credentials such as OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or GENAI_USERNAME and GENAI_PASSWORD when required.
Configure an MCP-compatible client to launch java -jar bindex-mcp-server-1.4.2.jar --projectDir /path/to/project.
Use the connected client to retrieve Bindex metadata, register a bindex.json document, or request library recommendations.

examples.title: Run an HTTP MCP service for team automation
examples.description: This scenario runs the packaged component as an HTTP MCP service that remote automation or team clients can invoke.
steps: Download bindex-mcp-server-1.4.2.jar or build the project with Maven.
Configure repository and AI provider settings before startup when registration or semantic recommendation is required.
Configure an MCP-compatible HTTP client to connect to http://localhost:8080/mcp.
Add --session to the startup command when the client requires streamable session-aware HTTP transport.
Invoke Bindex retrieval, registration, and recommendation operations to maintain artifact metadata and discover libraries matching stated development needs.
